core_obligations: Read the hypotheses on the cone (proof lines 11864-11865): the conditions that H^j(f) is an isomorphism for j > a and surjective for j = a say exactly that the cone C(f)^bullet has vanishing cohomology sheaves in degrees at least a.

Apply the local triviality lemma (proof lines 11866-11869): since E^bullet is strictly perfect and vanishes below a, the cited lemma gives a covering {U_i -> U} over whose members the composite E^bullet -> F^bullet -> C(f)^bullet is homotopic to zero.

Lift through the triangle (proof lines 11869-11877): the triangle G^bullet -> F^bullet -> C(f)^bullet -> G^bullet[1] restricts to a distinguished triangle in K(O_{U_i}), so null-homotopy of the composite produces the required dotted arrow alpha_i : E^bullet|_{U_i} -> G^bullet|_{U_i} making the diagram commute up to homotopy.
proof_roadmap: Translate the hypotheses on H^j(f) into vanishing of the cohomology of the cone above degree a.
Use the local triviality of maps from a strictly perfect complex to get local null-homotopy of the composite with the cone map.
Apply the long exact sequence of homotopy classes for the cone triangle to produce the lift.
Collect the covering provided by the local triviality lemma.
difficulty_reason: The lemma lifts a map alpha : E^bullet -> F^bullet from a strictly perfect complex through a quasi-isomorphism-like map f : G^bullet -> F^bullet, locally up to homotopy (statement lines 11847-11861). The proof consists of a translation and a triangle argument: the hypotheses on H^j(f) are recognised as the vanishing of the cohomology sheaves of the cone C(f)^bullet in degrees at least a (proof lines 11864-11865), which lets the same-chapter local triviality lemma supply a covering over whose members the composite with the cone map is null-homotopic (proof lines 11866-11869), after which the distinguished triangle attached to the cone turns that null-homotopy into the required lift (proof lines 11869-11877). The non-formal point is the passage from null-homotopy of a composite to a lift. The claim is H2: two standard inputs combined in the right order.
